Hi Liam / Sophie,

Thanks again for taking the call today — good to get a sense of Acme Cloud's roadmap. Quick recap from our side and a couple of follow-ups so we can produce a tailored hosted-API estimate: 

Recap / ask: 
- Expected steady-state monthly token volume: ~60M-80M tokens (you mentioned ~75M as a mid-point).
- Peak TPS: spikes up to ~35-45 TPS for ~10-20 minutes during promotional events. Typical baseline TPS ~5-10.
- Target unit economics: you mentioned wanting to be around $200 per 1M tokens (ballpark).
- Initial monthly budget range: $12k	6k (you said this is the current budget bucket for the pilot).

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Ill pull together a hosted-API estimate showing both pay-as-you-go and a reserved/committed discount that helps with predictable peaks.
2) Marissa — can you add a quick capacity note on handling 45 TPS bursts and whether we recommend a Dedicated or Hosted + burst plan?
3) Well include an example cost run for 75M tokens at $/1M tiers to make the monthly math explicit.

I attached a short estimate template so you can see how the math looks. Can you confirm the 75M figure and whether promotional spikes are typically no longer than 30 minutes? Also flag any compliance needs we should be aware of.

Thanks — speak soon.

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — monthly tokens & peak TPS

Thanks Ben — quick clarifications: 

- 75M/month is our best estimate for the pilot if usage grows as expected. Could be 60M in month 1, ramping to ~80M by month 3.
- Peak TPS: we saw 35 TPS on last promo but expect the next event could reach ~40 TPS, maybe up to 45 TPS for short windows (5-20 minutes).
- Budget: given other line items, we were hoping for a hosted rate that gets us to roughly $150	30 per 1M tokens. Our target internal forecast uses $200/1M as the planning number. That would put pilot monthly cost around $15k (75 * $200).
- SLA / burst: we need to understand whether hosted can sustain 40	45 TPS bursts without queuing or whether we should discuss reserved capacity.

If you can share a sample monthly math and an estimate for both hosted and reserved (committed) options, we can take it to procurement. Also, can you confirm data isolation & basic SOC2 evidence (we have that on a checklist)?

Appreciate it — Liam

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — monthly tokens & peak TPS

Liam — great, that's super helpful. Attached is a quick hosted vs reserved estimate for 75M tokens that shows the monthly math and a couple of model-rate assumptions. Highlights: 

- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): example tier at $225 per 1M tokens (reflects a mid-range model choice); 75M -> $16,875/month. Includes on-demand scaling for bursts but subject to short-term queuing if overall region capacity is tight.
- Committed/Reserved: 12-month commit example gives ~20% discount (~$180 per 1M), so 75M -> $13,500/month and stronger guarantee on capacity during spikes.
- Peak TPS handling: for short 40—45 TPS bursts we recommend either (a) Hosted + burst capacity (we can enable short-term autoscaling for events) or (b) Reserved pool sized to cover expected peak with a small buffer. Marissa has added the sizing note below.
- Cost-reduction levers: batching, prefix caching, and a slightly lower-capacity model variant for non-interactive flows can drop effective $/1M by 10–30% depending on workload.

See attached spreadsheet for line-by-line math and a sample SOW draft if you want procurement language.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa/Alex to confirm that reserved pool sizing for 45 TPS (with 20% buffer) is N GPUs X (internal sizing).
- If that looks good, schedule a 30-min pricing/ops call next week to walk procurement through the SOW and capacity plan.

Ben

Quick sizing note from eng/solutions: 

- For ~75M tokens/month with 40—45 TPS short bursts, recommended configuration is Hosted with burst autoscaling for the pilot. If Acme wants guaranteed latency during spikes, Reserved capacity sized for 45 TPS + 20% buffer is the safer option.
- Rough GPU sizing: reserved pool equivalent to 4x A100-class instances (or 6x smaller T4/GBv2 depending on model) for the peak profile; we’ll confirm exact numbers once we lock model and average sequence length.

I'll update the estimate spreadsheet with the reserved-pool math and a line showing the effective $/1M under both scenarios. Ben — I'll be available to join the procurement call next week.
